structure.title: Departure of Directors or Certain Officers; Election of Directors; Appointment of Certain Officers; Compensatory Arrangements of Certain Officers.
structure.heading: Item 5.02. Departure of Directors or Certain Officers; Election of Directors; Appointment of Certain Officers; Compensatory Arrangements of Certain Officers.
structure.start_phrase: On August 19, 2022, Foot Locker, Inc. (the “Company”), issued a press release announcing that, as part of a planned succession process, Richard A. Johnson will step down as President and Chief Executive Officer of the Company, effective September 1, 2022.
structure.summary:
- Foot Locker announced a planned CEO transition: Richard A. Johnson will step down as President and CEO effective September 1, 2022; Mary N. Dillon, former Ulta Beauty CEO/Executive Chair, is appointed President and CEO and joins the Board and its Executive Committee effective the same date. A press release (Exhibit 99.1) was issued.
- Ms. Dillon’s background includes senior roles at Ulta Beauty, U.S. Cellular, McDonald’s, and PepsiCo; she currently serves on the boards of Starbucks and KKR and previously served on Target’s board. She has no family relationships with company insiders and no related-party transactions requiring disclosure.
- Mr. Johnson entered a letter agreement (Exhibit 10.1) outlining his transition: Executive Chairman from September 1, 2022 to January 31, 2023, then Senior Advisor through a retirement date between April 1–15, 2023. He remains eligible for the 2022 bonus; his salary is reduced by 50% during the Senior Advisor period; he will not receive 2023 annual equity awards or participate in the 2023 bonus plan. His prior employment agreement otherwise remains materially unchanged.
- Ms. Dillon’s Employment Agreement (Exhibit 10.2) runs from August 19, 2022 through January 31, 2026 (auto-renewing annually), with a minimum $1.3 million base salary, participation in executive incentive/equity plans, a target annual bonus equal to 200% of base salary (prorated for 2022), and a $250,000 cash sign-on bonus.
- Inducement equity awards effective August 24, 2022: $2 million in RSUs vesting on the third anniversary; $5 million in “transformation” PSUs vesting based on three years and performance; and an annual $8 million grant (pro-rated for the current fiscal year) split 60% PSUs, 20% RSUs, 20% non-qualified stock options. These will be granted outside the 2007 Stock Incentive Plan as NYSE employment inducement awards (Rule 303A.08).
- Severance: If terminated without cause or for good reason, Ms. Dillon receives two years’ base salary continuation, a prorated bonus based on actual performance for the year of termination, and one year of outplacement. Equity vests per plan terms; for awards granted through March 2027, with Board consent, 50% vests if employment ends on/after the fiscal year ending around January 31, 2027, and 100% vests on/after the fiscal year ending around January 31, 2028. Upon a qualifying termination within two years after a change in control, she receives a lump sum equal to two times base salary plus target bonus within 10 days.
- Neither Mr. Johnson nor Ms. Dillon will receive additional compensation for Board or committee service.
- Exhibits: 10.1 (Johnson letter agreement), 10.2 (Dillon employment agreement), 99.1 (press release), and 104 (cover page iXBRL data).

structure.title: Letter Agreement, by and between Foot Locker, Inc. and Richard A. Johnson, dated August 17, 2022.
structure.heading: Exhibit 10.1
structure.start_phrase: In concert with the CEO succession planning process and the designation of a successor candidate, you have informed the Board of Directors of Foot Locker, Inc., a New York corporation with its principal office located at 330 West 34th Street, New York, New York 10001 (the “Company”) of your intent to retire from the Company.
structure.summary:
- Exhibit 10.1 is a letter agreement dated August 17, 2022 between Foot Locker, Inc. and Richard A. Johnson, executed to facilitate CEO succession and Johnson’s planned retirement and to ensure a smooth transition.
- It incorporates Johnson’s November 6, 2014 Senior Executive Employment Agreement by reference, with this new agreement controlling in the event of any conflict.
- Employment Transition Period terms:
  - Johnson will serve as President and Chief Executive Officer through August 31, 2022 (the Transition Date).
  - Effective September 1, 2022, he will serve as Executive Chairman through January 31, 2023 (the Executive Chairman Term).
  - Compensation and incentives during the Executive Chairman Term:
    - Continued monthly base pay at the current rate, paid per company practices.
    - Eligibility for the full 2022 bonus under the Foot Locker Executive Incentive Cash Compensation Plan (without proration), payable no later than 2.5 months after fiscal year-end.
    - Continued vesting of outstanding awards under the 2007 Stock Incentive Plan according to existing award terms.
  - During the Executive Chairman Term, he will serve full time as Executive Chairman, reporting to the Board (further details truncated).

nodes.title: Employment Transition Period.
nodes.heading: 1. Employment Transition Period.
nodes.start_phrase: You and the Company hereby agree to the following in respect of your retirement from the Company, its subsidiaries, and other corporate affiliates (collectively, the “Employer”):
nodes.summary:
- Exhibit 10.1 is a Letter Agreement dated August 17, 2022, between Foot Locker, Inc. and Richard A. Johnson, documenting his planned retirement as part of the CEO succession process and setting terms for a smooth transition.
- The agreement incorporates the November 6, 2014 Senior Executive Employment Agreement by reference, and states that this Letter Agreement controls in the event of any conflict.
- Employment transition:
  - Johnson will remain President and Chief Executive Officer through August 31, 2022 (the Transition Date).
  - He will then serve as Executive Chairman from September 1, 2022 through January 31, 2023 (the Executive Chairman Term), continuing in a full-time capacity and reporting to the Board of Directors.
- Compensation and incentives during the Executive Chairman Term:
  - He will continue to receive his current monthly base pay per the company’s standard payroll practices.
  - He remains eligible for his full, non-prorated 2022 bonus under the Foot Locker Executive Incentive Cash Compensation Plan, payable no later than 2.5 months after the end of fiscal 2022.
  - He will continue to vest in outstanding awards under the Company’s 2007 Stock Incentive Plan according to their existing terms.
- The agreement applies to Johnson’s retirement from the Company and its subsidiaries and affiliates (collectively, the Employer), and is intended to recognize his service and ensure an orderly leadership transition.

nodes.title: Service as Executive Chairman.
nodes.heading: (a) Service as Executive Chairman.
nodes.start_phrase: You shall continue to serve as President and Chief Executive Officer of the Company through August 31, 2022 (the “Transition Date”).
nodes.summary:
- Letter Agreement (Exhibit 10.1) dated August 17, 2022 between Foot Locker, Inc. and Richard A. Johnson to manage CEO succession and Johnson’s retirement; incorporates the 2014 Senior Executive Employment Agreement but controls in case of conflict.
- Role timeline:
  - President & CEO through August 31, 2022 (Transition Date).
  - Executive Chairman from September 1, 2022 to January 31, 2023.
  - Senior Advisor from February 1, 2023 to a mutually agreed Separation Date between April 1 and April 15, 2023.
- Executive Chairman duties: full-time role reporting to the Board; coordinate with the Lead Independent Director; consult with the CEO on financial, operational, commercial, legal/public reporting, and administrative matters; assist with transition of responsibilities.
- Executive Chairman compensation/benefits: continue monthly base salary at current level; eligible for full-year 2022 bonus under the Executive Incentive Cash Compensation Plan (no proration), payable within 2.5 months after FY2022 end; continued vesting of outstanding awards under the 2007 Stock Incentive Plan; no eligibility for a 2023 bonus and no additional equity grants.
- Senior Advisor compensation/benefits: monthly base pay at 50% of current base; continued vesting of outstanding equity awards under the Stock Incentive Plan.
- Section 409A intent: During both the Executive Chairman and Senior Advisor terms, service level to exceed 20% of the prior 36-month average to avoid a “separation from service” for nonqualified deferred compensation purposes.

nodes.title: Service as Senior Advisor.
nodes.heading: (b) Service as Senior Advisor.
nodes.start_phrase: Commencing February 1, 2023, you will assume the role of Senior Advisor and will continue in such role through a date to be mutually agreed upon by you and the Non-Executive Chair of the Company, which date shall be no earlier than April 1, 2023 and no later than April 15, 2023 (the “Separation Date” and such term, the “Senior Advisor Term”).
nodes.summary:
- Executive transition and duties: The executive will serve as Executive Chairman, chairing the Board, coordinating with the Lead Independent Director, consulting with the CEO on financial, operational, commercial, legal (including public company reporting), and administrative matters, and assisting with transition of current responsibilities to the CEO.
- Compensation/awards during Executive Chairman term: No eligibility for a 2023 Bonus Plan grant and no additional equity grants after the agreement date. Service level intended to exceed 20% of the average over the prior 36 months to avoid a “separation from service” under Section 409A for nonqualified deferred compensation plans.
- Senior Advisor term: Begins February 1, 2023 and ends on a mutually agreed date between April 1 and April 15, 2023 (the Separation Date). Monthly base pay equals 50% of the base pay in effect immediately prior to the agreement date, paid per company practices. Continued vesting of existing equity awards under the Stock Incentive Plan per their terms. Service level during this term also intended to exceed 20% for Section 409A purposes.
- Office and support: Office and suitable administrative support provided at the employer’s St. Petersburg, Florida office during both roles.
- Benefits: Continued eligibility for specified employee benefits and fringe benefits per Sections 5(c)(i), (v), and (vi) of the Employment Agreement.
- Separation/retirement: Employment terminates on the Separation Date due to retirement, unless earlier death or termination for Cause. The executive waives any right to resign for Good Reason. Any termination by the Company other than for Cause during the Executive Chairman or Senior Advisor terms constitutes a breach, entitling the executive to benefits under Section 8(d) of the Employment Agreement, subject to its conditions.
- Post-termination obligations: The Employment Agreement’s Non-Competition and Confidentiality provision remains in effect. A non-solicitation of employees covenant applies during employment and for two years from the Separation Date.
- Cooperation: For two years post-Separation Date, the executive will reasonably cooperate on matters related to prior service upon reasonable notice; the employer will reimburse reasonable expenses (excluding legal fees) associated with such cooperation.

nodes.title: Office and Administrative Assistance.
nodes.heading: (c) Office and Administrative Assistance.
nodes.start_phrase: While you are serving as Executive Chairman and Senior Advisor, the Employer will provide you with an office and suitable administrative support services at the Employer’s office in St. Petersburg, Florida.
nodes.summary:

- Provides office space and appropriate administrative support in the employer’s St. Petersburg, Florida office during the Executive Chairman and Senior Advisor roles.
- Establishes that employment will end on the Separation Date due to retirement unless earlier terminated by death or by the employer for Cause; the executive waives the right to resign for Good Reason.
- States that any termination by the company other than for Cause during the Executive Chairman or Senior Advisor terms is a breach, triggering benefits under Employment Agreement Section 8(d), subject to its conditions.
- Affirms that the Employment Agreement’s Non-Competition and Confidentiality provision (paragraph 9) remains in effect.
- Imposes a non-solicitation of employees covenant for the remainder of employment and for two years following the Separation Date.
- Requires cooperation by the executive for two years after the Separation Date on matters related to prior service, with reimbursement of reasonable expenses (excluding legal fees).

nodes.title: Benefits and Fringe Benefits.
nodes.heading: (d) Benefits and Fringe Benefits.
nodes.start_phrase: While you are serving as Executive Chairman and Senior Advisor, you will continue to be eligible to participate in the Company’s employee benefit programs and fringe benefits as set forth in Sections 5(c)(i), (v) and (vi) of the Employment Agreement.
nodes.summary:
- While serving as Executive Chairman and Senior Advisor, the employer will provide an office and suitable administrative support at the St. Petersburg, Florida office.
- During this period, the executive remains eligible to participate in specified company benefit programs and fringe benefits per Sections 5(c)(i), (v), and (vi) of the Employment Agreement, with a reference to treatment under any employer nonqualified deferred compensation plan.
- On the Separation Date, employment will terminate due to retirement unless earlier ended by death or for Cause; the executive waives any right to resign for Good Reason.
- Any termination by the company other than for Cause during the Executive Chairman or Senior Advisor terms constitutes a breach, entitling the executive to benefits under Section 8(d) of the Employment Agreement, subject to its conditions.
- Post-termination obligations include:
  - The existing Non-Competition and Confidentiality provisions (Employment Agreement, paragraph 9) remain fully in effect.
  - A non-solicitation covenant prohibiting solicitation, hiring, or inducing departure of employer employees during the remainder of employment and for two years following the Separation Date.
- Cooperation clause: for two years after the Separation Date, upon reasonable request and notice, the executive will cooperate on matters related to prior service; the employer will reimburse reasonable expenses (excluding legal fees) incurred for such cooperation.

nodes.title: Retirement Date.
nodes.heading: (e) Retirement Date.
nodes.start_phrase: You acknowledge and agree that on the Separation Date, your employment with Employer will terminate by reason of your retirement unless earlier (1) terminated by reason of your death, or (2) terminated by the Employer for Cause (as defined in the Employment Agreement).
nodes.summary:

- Provides office space and administrative support at the employer’s St. Petersburg, Florida office during the Executive Chairman/Senior Advisor period.
- Confirms continued eligibility for certain employee benefit programs and fringe benefits as referenced in Sections 5(c)(i), (v), and (vi) of the Employment Agreement.
- Defines the Separation Date as a retirement termination unless earlier ended by death or for Cause; the executive waives the right to resign for Good Reason.
- States that any termination by the Company other than for Cause during the Executive Chairman or Senior Advisor terms constitutes a breach, triggering benefits under Section 8(d) of the Employment Agreement, subject to its conditions.
- Affirms that the Employment Agreement’s Non-Competition and Confidentiality provisions (paragraph 9) remain in effect.
- Imposes a non-solicitation of employees restriction during the remainder of employment and for two years after the Separation Date.
- Requires the executive to cooperate for two years post-Separation on matters related to prior service upon reasonable request and notice, with reimbursement of reasonable expenses (excluding legal fees).
- References applicability for purposes of any Employer nonqualified deferred compensation plan (context truncated).

nodes.title: Post-Termination Obligations and Restrictive Covenants.
nodes.heading: 2. Post-Termination Obligations and Restrictive Covenants.
nodes.start_phrase: (a) The “Non-Competition and Confidentiality” provision of the Employment Agreement, paragraph 9, will remain outstanding and not be impacted by the execution of this Agreement.
nodes.summary:

- Employer to provide an office and appropriate administrative support at the St. Petersburg, Florida location during the Executive Chairman and Senior Advisor terms.
- Executive remains eligible for specified Company employee benefit programs and fringe benefits (as referenced in Sections 5(c)(i), (v), and (vi) of the Employment Agreement) while serving in those roles.

nodes.title: Non-Solicitation of Employees.
nodes.heading: (b) Non-Solicitation of Employees.
nodes.start_phrase: You understand and acknowledge that the Employer has expended and continues to expend significant time and expense in recruiting and training its employees and that the loss of employees would cause significant and irreparable harm to the Employer.
nodes.summary:
- Describes transition terms for an executive serving as Executive Chairman and Senior Advisor, including continued participation in certain company benefit and fringe benefit programs referenced in the Employment Agreement.
- Provides that while serving in these roles, the employer will furnish an office and suitable administrative support at the St. Petersburg, Florida office.
- Establishes the Separation Date as the retirement date unless earlier terminated due to death or for Cause (as defined in the Employment Agreement); the executive waives the right to resign for Good Reason.
- States that any termination by the company other than for Cause during the Executive Chairman Term or Senior Advisor Term breaches the agreement and entitles the executive to the payments/benefits in Section 8(d) of the Employment Agreement, subject to its conditions.
- Confirms that the Employment Agreement’s Non-Competition and Confidentiality provision (paragraph 9) remains in force and is unaffected by this new agreement.
- Imposes a non-solicitation covenant prohibiting direct or indirect solicitation, hiring, or inducement of the employer’s employees during employment and for two years following the Separation Date.
- Requires the executive to cooperate, upon reasonable request and notice, for two years after the Separation Date on matters related to prior service, with reimbursement of reasonable expenses (excluding legal fees).
- References participation in an employer nonqualified deferred compensation plan.

nodes.title: Cooperation.
nodes.heading: 3. Cooperation.
nodes.start_phrase: You and the Employer agree that certain matters in which you have been involved during your employment may need your cooperation with the Employer in the future.
nodes.summary:
- Confirms provision of an office and administrative support in St. Petersburg, Florida while serving as Executive Chairman and Senior Advisor.
- Continues eligibility for specified Company benefit and fringe benefit programs per Employment Agreement Sections 5(c)(i), (v), and (vi).
- Establishes that employment ends on the Separation Date due to retirement unless earlier death or termination for Cause; waives the right to resign for Good Reason; provides that any termination other than for Cause during the Executive Chairman or Senior Advisor terms is a breach entitling the employee to Section 8(d) benefits (subject to conditions).
- Maintains existing non-competition and confidentiality obligations from the Employment Agreement; adds a non-solicitation of employees restriction during employment and for two years after the Separation Date.
- Requires cooperation for two years post-Separation Date on matters related to prior service, with reimbursement of reasonable expenses (excluding legal fees) and additional compensation if total cooperation exceeds 20 hours, calculated from base salary at the Separation Date.
- Imposes mutual non-disparagement: the employee will not make defamatory or maliciously false public statements about the Company or its people; the Company will instruct senior management and the Board to avoid disparaging the employee. Carves out protected rights (e.g., NLRA, securities laws, Dodd-Frank) and legal compliance obligations, with a requirement to provide prompt notice to the General Counsel if compelled by order.
- Continues indemnification protections during the Executive Chairman and Senior Advisor terms to the same extent as previously provided, in addition to D&O coverage.
- Provides reimbursement of up to $25,000 for reasonable legal fees related to preparing and negotiating the agreement (subject to Section 11).
- Sets assignment terms: the Employer may assign; the employee may not; binds successors and assigns.
- Specifies New York law as governing law and sets jurisdiction/venue for matters arising out of the agreement and employment/termination.
- States that the agreement is the entire understanding regarding separation and supersedes prior discussions and agreements on that subject, except as otherwise specifically provided.

nodes.title: Certain Communications.
nodes.heading: 4. Certain Communications.
nodes.start_phrase: You agree that you shall not at any time engage in, make, publish, or communicate to any person or entity in any public forum any defamatory or maliciously false remarks, comments, or statements (“Disparaging Conduct”) concerning the Employer or its businesses, or any of its employees, officers, or directors.
nodes.summary:
- Post-separation cooperation: For two years after the Separation Date, the employee will cooperate; if cooperation exceeds 20 total hours, the employer will pay an hourly/per-diem fee based on the employee’s base salary for documented time.
- Non-disparagement: The employee will not make defamatory or maliciously false statements about the employer, its business, or its people. Carve-outs preserve protected rights (e.g., NLRA, Dodd-Frank/SEC) and compliance with lawful orders, with a requirement to promptly notify the General Counsel. The company will instruct and use reasonable efforts to ensure senior management and the Board do not disparage the employee.
- Indemnification: During the Executive Chairman Term and Senior Advisor Term, the company will indemnify the employee to the same extent as when serving as President and CEO, in addition to D&O insurance coverage.
- Legal fees: The company will reimburse reasonable fees for preparing and negotiating the agreement, up to $25,000 (subject to Section 11).
- Assignment: The employer may freely assign the agreement; the employee may not, and any attempted assignment by the employee is void.
- Governing law: New York law governs the agreement and all related employment/termination matters, without regard to conflicts-of-law rules.
- Entire agreement: The agreement supersedes prior understandings regarding the separation except as specifically provided; the clause appears to continue beyond the provided excerpt.

nodes.title: Governing Law, Jurisdiction, and Venue.
nodes.heading: 8. Governing Law, Jurisdiction, and Venue.

nodes.title: Position and Duties.
nodes.heading: 2. Position and Duties.
nodes.start_phrase: (a) From the Commencement Date through August 31, 2022, Executive shall serve in a non-executive advisory capacity.
nodes.summary:
- Parties: Employment agreement between Foot Locker, Inc. and Mary N. Dillon (the Executive).
- Role and start: Executive to serve first in a non-executive advisory capacity from August 19–31, 2022, then as President and Chief Executive Officer effective September 1, 2022, reporting solely to the Board.
- Board seat: Executive to be elected to the Company’s Board within 30 days of the Commencement Date.
- Term: Initial Term from August 19, 2022 through January 31, 2026, with automatic one-year renewals unless either party gives 180 days’ notice; term aligns with the Company’s fiscal year if it changes.
- Duties: Full-time devotion to Company business (subject to limited permitted outside activities) with responsibilities commensurate with a CEO; must comply with Company policies and Corporate Governance Guidelines.
- Additional roles: Executive may be asked to serve as an officer/director of subsidiaries and affiliates; automatic resignation from all positions upon termination of employment, with cooperation to execute related documents.
- Permitted outside activities: With Board approval/conditions—service on one other public or substantial private company board; advisory roles to up to two private companies with minimal time; service on trade association/charitable boards; charitable/community work; management of personal investments—provided no conflict, no material interference, and compliance with noncompetition/confidentiality (Section 7 referenced).

- Cash compensation: Base salary of at least $1,300,000 per year, paid in substantially equal monthly installments; subject to annual review by the Compensation Committee.

nodes.title: Place of Performance.
nodes.heading: 3. Place of Performance.
nodes.start_phrase: Executive shall provide services from an office of the Company or one of its subsidiaries in the Chicago, Illinois area, provided Executive shall be required to travel in connection with her employment, commensurate with the activities of her position.
nodes.summary:

- Compliance: Executive must adhere to Company rules, policies, directions, and restrictions applicable to officers/employees, including Foot Locker, Inc. Corporate Governance Guidelines.
- Place of performance: Primary office in the Chicago, Illinois area, with travel as appropriate for the role.
- Cash compensation: Base salary set by the Board’s Compensation Committee, reviewed at least annually, not less than $1,300,000 per year, paid in substantially equal monthly installments.
- Incentive participation: Eligibility to participate in Company bonus, incentive, and equity plans for comparably situated senior executives, subject to plan terms; Company may amend or terminate such plans if changes apply broadly and do not disproportionately reduce Executive’s rights or benefits.

nodes.title: Cash Compensation.
nodes.heading: 4. Cash Compensation.
nodes.start_phrase: (a) During the Employment Period, the Company shall pay Executive a base salary at such rate per year as may be fixed by the Human Capital and Compensation Committee of the Board (the “Compensation Committee”) from time to time (and shall be reviewed at least annually by the Compensation Committee), but in no event at a rate of less than $1,300,000 per year, to be paid in substantially equal monthly installments, in accordance with the normal payroll practices of the Company (the “Base Salary”).
nodes.summary:
- Automatic resignations: Executive automatically resigns from positions with any subsidiary upon termination and agrees to execute any additional documents requested by the Company.
- Permitted outside activities: Executive may (with specified Board approvals and subject to fiduciary duties) serve on one other public/substantial private company board, advise up to two private companies with minimal time, serve on trade/charitable boards, engage in charitable/community activities, and manage personal investments—provided these do not violate Section 7 or materially interfere with duties and comply with Company policies and Corporate Governance Guidelines.
- Place of performance: Primary office in the Chicago, Illinois area, with travel as required for the role.
- Cash compensation:
  - Base salary: At least $1,300,000 per year, reviewed at least annually, paid in equal monthly installments.
  - Incentives: Participation in Company bonus, incentive, and equity plans for similarly situated senior executives; plans may be amended/terminated if applied uniformly and without disproportionate impact on Executive.
  - Annual bonus: Target opportunity equal to 200% of Base Salary under the AICP during the Employment Period; exception for fiscal year ending January 28, 2023—Executive receives a prorated bonus (not under the AICP) of at least the prorated portion of 200% of Base Salary or, if higher, the prorated amount based on actual performance.
- Inducement and equity awards:
  - RSUs: Granted August 24, 2022 with a value of $2,000,000 (number based on closing price that day); cliff vest 100% on the third anniversary of the Commencement Date, subject to continued service; governed by an Employment Inducement Award Agreement.
  - Transformation Award (PSUs): Granted August 24, 2022 with a value of $5,000,000 (number based on closing price that day); metrics/targets set by the Compensation Committee with Executive input no later than March 2023 (the Determination Date); service-based vesting occurs 100% on the third anniversary of the Determination Date; performance vesting criteria finalized by the Compensation Committee after issuance of audited financials; subject to an Employment Inducement Award Agreement.

nodes.title: Inducement and Equity Awards.
nodes.heading: 5. Inducement and Equity Awards.
nodes.start_phrase: Also as an inducement to commence employment with the Company, on August 24, 2022, Executive shall be granted a number of restricted stock units (“RSUs”) with respect to Company Common Stock, par value $0.01 per share (“Company Stock”) determined by dividing $2,000,000 by the closing price of a share of Company Stock on August 24, 2022.
nodes.summary:
- Annual Bonus: Target annual bonus equal to 200% of Base Salary under the AICP during the Employment Period. For the fiscal year ending January 28, 2023, Executive will not participate in the AICP; instead, a pro-rated bonus from Commencement through January 28, 2023 will be paid by the 15th day of the third month after January 28, 2023, equal to at least the pro-rated portion of 200% of Base Salary or, if higher, the pro-rated actual-performance amount.
- Inducement RSUs: Grant on August 24, 2022 with a value of $2,000,000 (shares determined by dividing by the closing price on that date). Vests 100% on the third anniversary of the Commencement Date, subject to continued service; subject to an Employment Inducement Award Agreement.
- Transformation Award (PSUs): Grant on August 24, 2022 with a value of $5,000,000 (shares based on the closing price on that date). Metrics/targets set by the Compensation Committee with Executive input by March 2023 (Determination Date). Service vesting: 100% on the third anniversary of the Determination Date. Performance vesting determined after audited financials (March 2026). Settlement timed to comply with Section 409A.
- Pro-Rata Initial Annual Equity Award: Grant date value of $8,000,000, pro-rated from Commencement to January 28, 2023: 60% PSUs (same conditions as other senior officers), 20% stock options (vesting 1/3 on each of the first three anniversaries), 20% RSUs (cliff vest on the third anniversary). PSUs/RSUs share count based on August 24, 2022 closing price; options based on Black-Scholes; subject to an Employment Inducement Award Agreement.
- Ongoing Annual Equity Awards: From fiscal 2023, eligibility under the Company’s Stock Plan with a target annual long-term incentive value of at least $8,000,000; terms generally consistent with other senior officers, except as modified by special vesting provisions.
- Special Vesting Provisions (for awards granted through March 2027):
  - Voluntary termination with Board consent on/after the fiscal year ending around January 31, 2027: 50% of then-outstanding unvested equity awards vest (time-based at termination; performance-based at end of performance period based on actual results; settlements comply with Section 409A).
  - Voluntary termination with Board consent on/after the fiscal year ending around January 31, 2028: 100% of then-outstanding unvested equity awards vest (same mechanics).
  - Death or Disability: All then-outstanding unvested equity awards vest (same mechanics).
- Sign-On Bonus: $250,000 cash, payable within 30 days of commencement.
- Additional Benefits: Eligibility for standard senior-executive benefit plans and perquisites, including company-paid life insurance equal to Base Salary, long-term disability coverage of $25,000/month, up to $7,500/year reimbursement of out-of-pocket medical expenses, and a $20,000 annual financial planning/tax advisory allowance; no car allowance. Expense reimbursements subject to Company policies (section incomplete).

nodes.title: Additional Benefits.
nodes.heading: 6. Additional Benefits.
nodes.start_phrase: (a) During the Employment Period, Executive shall be eligible to participate in all pension, welfare, and fringe benefit plans, as well as perquisites, maintained by the Company from time to time for its comparably situated senior executives in accordance with their respective terms as in effect from time to time.
nodes.summary:
- Equity award vesting rules upon certain terminations:
  - Time-based awards vest upon employment termination; performance awards vest at the end of the performance period based on actual results and settle in a manner compliant with Section 409A.
  - If the Executive voluntarily resigns with Board consent on or after the fiscal year ending on or about January 31, 2028, 100% of then-outstanding, unvested equity vests (with the same time-based/performance award timing and 409A compliance).
  - If employment ends due to death or disability (Sections 7(a)(i) or (ii)), all then-outstanding, unvested equity vests with the same mechanics and 409A compliance.
- Sign-on bonus: $250,000 cash, payable within 30 days of employment commencement.
- Additional benefits during employment:
  - Eligibility to participate in company pension, welfare, fringe benefit plans, and perquisites offered to comparably situated senior executives (defined as Senior Vice President or higher).
  - Company-paid life insurance equal to annual Base Salary.
  - Long-term disability insurance of $25,000 per month.
  - Annual out-of-pocket medical expense reimbursement up to $7,500.
  - Annual $20,000 allowance for financial planning/tax advisory.
  - No car allowance.
- Expense reimbursement:
  - Reimbursement of reasonable business, entertainment, and travel expenses per company policy, including reasonable New York-area car service while in New York on company business.
  - Executive bears lodging and other personal expenses (e.g., non-business meals) while working at the New York principal office.
- Vacation: 20 days per calendar year (prorated for partial years); unused days are forfeited.
- Legal fees: Company reimburses reasonable legal fees and disbursements for negotiating/preparing the agreement and ancillary documents, capped at $40,000 and subject to Section 14(b).
- Termination provisions:
  - Triggers include death; disability (absence for 180 days with failure to return to full-time duties within 30 days after written notice); and termination for Cause.
  - “Cause” includes: refusal or willful failure to substantially perform duties (with a 10-business-day cure after written notice); material dishonesty, willful misconduct, misappropriation, breach of fiduciary duty, or fraud; willful breach of a material provision of the agreement (10-business-day cure); and conviction of a felony or other crime involving moral turpitude (text truncated).

nodes.title: Termination.
nodes.heading: 7. Termination.
nodes.start_phrase: If the Company shall terminate the employment of Executive pursuant to the provisions of paragraph (a)(i), (ii) or (iii) above, it shall have no further liability or obligation hereunder except (i) to pay promptly to Executive her then-current Base Salary through the Termination Date, (ii) to provide reimbursement for reasonable and necessary expenses incurred by Executive through the date of notice of such termination of employment, to the extent otherwise provided under Section 6(b) above; and (iii) all other vested payments and benefits to which Executive may otherwise be entitled pursuant to the terms of the applicable Company benefit plan or arrangement through the effective date of such termination of employment ((i), (ii) and (iii), the (“Accrued Benefits”)).
nodes.summary:
- Expense reimbursement and perks: The executive will be promptly reimbursed for reasonable business, entertainment, and travel expenses, including use of a car service in the New York metropolitan area while on Company business. She is responsible for lodging and personal expenses while working at the Company’s New York principal office.
- Time off: 20 vacation days per calendar year, prorated for partial years; unused days are forfeited.
- Legal fees: Reimbursement of reasonable legal fees and disbursements incurred in negotiating and preparing the agreement and related documents, capped at $40,000 (subject to Section 14(b)).
- Definition: “Comparably situated senior executives” means corporate officers at Senior Vice President level or higher.

- Termination events (Section 7):
  - Automatic upon death or after specified disability period (180 days of absence with 30-day notice and no return).
  - By the Company for Cause (including willful failure to perform duties after notice and cure period, dishonesty/misconduct/fraud, willful material breach after notice and cure, felony or crime of moral turpitude, or refusal to follow lawful Board directions after notice and cure).
  - By the Company without Cause (including non-renewal treated as without Cause at term end).
  - By the Executive without Good Reason or with Good Reason on 30 days’ notice (with Company cure/make-whole right for Good Reason prior to a Change in Control).

- Payments upon termination:
  - Death, disability, or for Cause: Accrued Benefits only (base salary through termination date, reimbursable expenses through notice date, and vested plan benefits); all other rights/obligations end (subject to Section 7(e)).
  - Without Cause by Company, or by Executive for Good Reason, or Company material breach (after cure period and timely resignation): In addition to Accrued Benefits, 24 months of base salary continuation; prorated annual bonus for the fiscal year of termination based on actual performance and paid with other officers; equity per plan/award terms or if more favorable per Section 5(e); one year of outplacement at senior-executive level. Payments subject to Section 409A timing (salary starts on day 60 or, if needed, after six-month delay with catch-up). No mitigation or offset. Eligibility requires timely execution and non-revocation of a release (within 21 days), cooperation in litigation, and compliance with Section 9.
  - Change in Control (within two years post-CIC): If terminated without Cause or for Good Reason, in lieu of the above severance, a lump sum equal to 2x (base salary + target annual bonus) paid within 10 days of termination (subject to Section 14(b)). Good Reason includes material demotion/diminution, base salary reduction, target bonus reduction, post-CIC benefit reductions without materially similar substitutes (subject to legal/broad-based exceptions with economic make-whole), failure of successor to assume, or other uncured material breach.

- 280G excise tax mitigation (Section 7(e)): Total Payments are reduced, if and only if doing so yields a greater after-tax amount, to $1 below the 280G threshold. Determination at Company expense by nationally recognized consultants, considering factors such as noncompetition value; with a specified order of reductions across cash, equity, and non-cash benefits.

- Indemnification and D&O insurance: Executive is entitled to indemnification per the Company’s charter/bylaws during and after employment for actions as an officer/director. The Company will maintain directors’ and officers’ liability insurance during employment (if reasonably priced) and thereafter for prior activities at levels maintained for active directors/officers. An indemnification agreement in standard form will be executed as of the commencement date.

- Confidential information and non-competition (Section 9): Ongoing obligation not to disclose or use nonpublic Company information (financials, strategies, operations, personnel, customers, real estate, etc.) except as permitted or required by law/court order; commitment to comply with the Company’s Code of Business Conduct. Includes notice of whistleblower immunity under 18 U.S.C. § 1833(b) for certain trade secret disclosures (provision continues beyond the excerpt).

nodes.title: Indemnification.
nodes.heading: 8. Indemnification.
nodes.start_phrase: The Company agrees that the Executive shall be entitled to the benefits of the indemnity provisions set forth in the Certificate of Incorporation and the By-laws from time to time in accordance with their terms both during her employment and thereafter with regard to her actions as an officer or director of the Company.
nodes.summary:
- Golden parachute cutback mechanics under IRC Section 280G: establishes a waterfall to reduce payments/benefits to avoid excise tax, in this order—(i) equity-based payments valued at full value (highest values first), (ii) cash payments valued at less than full value (amounts payable last reduced first), (iii) equity valued at less than full value (highest values first), and (iv) remaining non-cash benefits reduced pro rata; values determined per Treasury Regulation Section 1.280G-1, Q&A 24.
- Indemnification: the Executive is entitled to indemnification under the Company’s Certificate of Incorporation and By-laws during and after employment for actions as an officer/director; the Company will maintain D&O liability insurance for the Executive during employment if reasonably priced and provide post-employment coverage for prior acts consistent with that for active directors/officers; the Company will enter into its standard Indemnification Agreement with the Executive effective on the Commencement Date.
- Confidentiality obligations: the Executive must not disclose or use nonpublic Company information during employment and thereafter, except with Company consent or as legally compelled; “Confidential Information” includes nonpublic financial data, plans, operations, personnel matters, distribution methods, supplier/customer and client relationships, marketing strategies, store lists, real estate strategies, and similar information; the Executive must comply with the Company’s Code of Business Conduct.
- Legal process exception: disclosure of Confidential Information is permitted when compelled by lawful process, subpoena, or court order, with limits as described.
- DTSA whistleblower notice: acknowledges immunity under 18 U.S.C. § 1833(b) for certain disclosures of trade secrets made in confidence to government officials or attorneys, or in court filings under seal (provision text partially shown).
- Section heading references “Confidential Information and Non-Competition,” though only confidentiality and DTSA notice provisions are detailed in the excerpt; specific non-competition terms are not included in the provided text.

nodes.title: Confidential Information and Non-Competition.
nodes.heading: 9. Confidential Information and Non-Competition.
nodes.start_phrase: (a) Executive agrees that during the Employment Period and thereafter she shall not disclose, at any time, to any person, or use for her own account, nonpublic information of any kind concerning the Company or any of its subsidiaries or affiliates, including, but not limited to, nonpublic information concerning finances, financial plans, accounting methods, strategic plans, operations, personnel, organizational structure, methods of distribution, suppliers, customers, client relationships, marketing strategies, store lists, real estate strategies, and the like (“Confidential Information”).
nodes.summary:
- Golden parachute cutback: Establishes an ordering rule to reduce payments subject to Internal Revenue Code Section 280G excise tax, prioritizing reductions by category and value per Treasury Regulation 1.280G-1, Q&A 24 (full-value equity first, then certain cash, then discounted-value equity, then other non-cash benefits pro rata).
- Indemnification and D&O insurance: Company will provide indemnification per its charter/bylaws, maintain directors’ and officers’ liability insurance during employment (and thereafter for prior acts as maintained for active officers/directors), and enter into a standard Indemnification Agreement as of the commencement date.
- Confidentiality: Executive must not disclose or use nonpublic Company information during and after employment, with allowances for disclosures compelled by law; must comply with the Company’s Code of Business Conduct.
- Whistleblower and legal carve-outs: Preserves rights under 18 U.S.C. § 1833(b) (DTSA immunity) and allows communications with government agencies (e.g., SEC, EEOC), personal counsel, participation in investigations, seeking SEC whistleblower awards, responding to subpoenas (with notice for protective orders), and disclosures needed to obtain public benefits.
- Non-compete and non-solicit: For two years post-employment, prohibits providing similar services to competitors of the Company’s “Athletic Business” or to major suppliers (≥$20M prior-year supply), within the U.S. or countries where the Company does business; excludes up to 1% passive public ownership and department/general merchandise stores. Bars soliciting/recruiting employees with whom the executive had dealings in the preceding 12 months if they in fact leave. Provides for injunctive relief and blue-penciling to enforce reasonable scope.
- Acknowledgments and consideration: Advises consulting counsel; provides a 14-day review period; confirms voluntary agreement and that benefits in Sections 4–6 are adequate consideration, including for purposes of the Illinois Freedom to Work Act.
- Assignment: Binds successors; executive cannot assign; Company may assign in a merger or asset sale if the successor assumes obligations.
- Arbitration: Most employment- and agreement-related disputes (including discrimination/harassment/retaliation) to be arbitrated in New York City under AAA rules; excludes certain restrictive covenant claims and allows, where required by law, court options for sexual harassment/assault claims.
